_rule: The estate accent palette. ENGINE — the set is shared; an estate's CHOICE is instance config, alongside display.defaultTextSize. `--accent` is the ONE token an instance overrides; --accent-on and --accent-ring derive from it (onboarding/index.html :69-81), which was NOT true before 2026-09-05.
_contrast: Ratios are NOT stored here on purpose — a typed ratio is a hand-kept fact that rots. `python3 tools/palette.py --check` recomputes every one from the hex and fails below AAA.
_ruled: [paul-ruled 2026-09-05] — 'include all of them, and yeah, include Fernwood as well.' Paul took the full candidate set over ux-expert's recommended five.  — AMENDED [paul-ruled 2026-09-06]: the swatch is now `fern` / "Fern". The original ruling stands as made and is kept above; it was made when Fernwood was the only estate. With a second household arriving, an engine-tier palette offering a swatch named after ONE household invited a new reader to paint their place after somebody else's house. tools/pages-deploy.py refused the first household export over exactly this. The HEX is unchanged, and an accent persists as a hex rather than an id, so no existing choice moves.
_known_trade: ⚠️ THREE GREENS (pine, spruce, fernwood) and a widened lightness band. ux-expert recommended ONE green and ONE blue because two of either is a discrimination task for a reader with documented difficulty reading, and proposed spruce as a SWAP for dusk rather than an addition; it flagged fernwood as outside the band (measured, not decided). Paul ruled the full set knowing this. Recorded as a KNOWN TRADE, not an oversight — if chip selection is later measured to be error-prone, this line is where to look first.
